coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 6 units (the domain directory itself plus 15.01, 15.02, 15.05, 15.06, 15.07) and 36 files — matches the expected 6 units / 36 files exactly. Every file was read in full and put through the 3a implementer simulation, 3b rubric scoring and 3c devil's-advocate pass. Rubric dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are scored N/A for every unit: this domain's files explicitly reference meta/personas.md ('Persona definitions live in meta/personas.md — referenced, never redefined here', gear-registry-ownership-index.md:67) and carry no budget, timeline, metric or competitor content, all of which live in meta/. Dimension 1 is scored against each unit index's 'Why this is a domain/sub-domain' rationale. Dimensions 1, 3, 7, 8 are therefore the applicable checkpoints per unit (4 each, 24 total). The 5 flat leaf features (15.03, 15.04, 15.08, 15.09, 15.10) have no index of their own and are audited as part of the domain-root unit. Roughly a dozen candidate findings were dropped on the devil's-advocate pass: stale [PENDING] markers whose substance is carried by a numbered open question elsewhere in the same file (15.01-cx:79 handshake timeout -> 15.01.03 Q-01; 15.01-cx:120 serial fork -> 15.01.06 Q-01; 15.02-cx:57 payout -> 15.02.01 Q-03; 15.02-cx:105 mid-checkout race -> 15.02.02 edge rows; 15.06.01:53/57 -> its Q-02/Q-03; 15.07.01:66 -> its Q-02; 15.07.03:69/70 -> its Q-02/Q-03), the 'active' vs 'reported' vocabulary drift at 15.02.02:56-57, the out-of-order D-numbering in 15.01.05, and the 15.01 index's mispointed 'see Q-02 in the domain index' note.

findings.claim: 15.09 Gear Discography specifies behaviour for a deleted/deregistered gear record and defers to '15.01.03 deletion/deregistration rules', but 15.01.01 D-10 locks the opposite — the record has no terminal state and deletion is not offered — and 15.01.03 (the transfer handshake) contains no deletion or deregistration rules at all.
findings.evidence: 15.09-gear-discography.md:73 — '| Gear record deleted/deregistered while it carries a discography | The session facts live in domain 02, not on the gear record; deletion cannot erase a credit. The gear identity is tombstoned, not vaporised | The credit still names the object; the object's own passport is gone or archived per 15.01 deletion rules |'. 15.09-gear-discography.md:102 — 'Depends on **15.01.01 Gear Record** ... and on **15.01.03 deletion/deregistration rules** for the tombstone case in the edge table.' Against 15.01-instrument-identity-provenance/15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:221 — 'D-10 | **The record has no terminal state.** "Destroyed" is an appended, reversible fact; deletion is not offered' and :118-119 — 'Deletion is not offered; erasure obligations are Q-04's problem, not a product affordance.' 15.01.03-ownership-transfer-handshake.md contains no deletion or deregistration text anywhere.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a gear record can be deregistered/tombstoned at all, and if so what state a tombstoned record holds and what its passport renders. An implementer following 15.01.01 D-10 builds no deletion path and treats the 15.09 row as unreachable; an implementer following 15.09 builds a tombstone/archive state for gear records. These are different products, and the pointer offered to reconcile them (15.01.03) is empty.

findings.claim: The domain index's Children table misstates the deepening status of 6 of its 10 children, misstates the total leaf-feature count, and asserts a blanket status that contradicts the child files themselves.
findings.evidence: gear-registry-ownership-index.md:29 — '10 children classified through the Node Classification Gate: **5 sub-domains** ... and **5 features** (leaf files). 21 leaf features total. All `[SURFACE]` pending Step 5 deepening.' The table's own Deep Think column sums to 6+4+3+3+3 = 19 sub-domain leaves plus 5 flat features = 24, not 21. Status column vs the target files' own headers: :37 '15.05 ... `[BREADTH]`' vs 15.05-valuation-appraisal-insurance-index.md:5 '**Status**: [SURFACE]'; :38 '15.06 ... `[BREADTH]`' vs 15.06-rig-profile-compatibility-index.md:5 '[SURFACE]'; :39 '15.07 ... `[BREADTH]`' vs 15.07-studio-backline-asset-register-index.md:5 '[SURFACE]'; :36 '15.04 ... `[SURFACE]`' vs 15.04-gear-collection-visibility.md:5 '[PARTIAL]'; :40 '15.08 ... `[SURFACE]`' vs 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:5 '[PARTIAL]'; :41 '15.09 ... `[SURFACE]`' vs 15.09-gear-discography.md:5 '[PARTIAL]'.
findings.forcedInvention: Which status is authoritative when a downstream stage gates on deepening state — the parent index or the child file. A reader trusting the index treats 15.04, 15.08 and 15.09 as un-deepened surface nodes needing another discovery pass, and treats 15.05/15.06/15.07 as breadth-complete when their own files say otherwise.

findings.claim: 15.01.05 D-03 ratifies that 15.01.05 authors the canonical identity-confidence value set and that 15.01.01 'never defines its own' — but 15.01.05 contains no value set anywhere, and 15.01.01 still carries the only enumeration on disk while flagging it as an unsettled proposal awaiting synthesis against a 15.01.05 set that does not exist.
findings.evidence: 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md:93 — 'D-03 | **DQ-MG-05:** this file **authors** the canonical identity-confidence value set; `15.01.01` renders it and never defines its own ... The values are the six already in use on disk'. No table or list of those six values appears anywhere in 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md; only two of them appear in passing prose (:45 'photo-bound, no serial', :57 'era-unknown'). Against 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:87-95, which is the only enumeration of the six ('| `serial-confirmed` | ... | `serial-typed` | ... | `serial-reconstructed` | ... | `photo-bound (no serial)` | ... | `era-unknown` | ... | `numbers-disagree` |'), followed at :96-98 by 'The vocabulary above is proposed from the render side and is flagged for Step 6 synthesis against 15.01.05's.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the identity-confidence vocabulary is settled and where it lives. One implementer takes 15.01.01's six values as canonical (per D-03's 'the values are the six already in use on disk'); another reads 15.01.01:98 literally, concludes there is a competing 15.01.05 set still to be synthesised, and blocks or invents one. The enum is the render contract for every gear record in the domain.

findings.claim: Within one file, the shared-serial discriminator is stated as an open question deferred to a future pass — naming three candidate answers — while that same file's Q-01 records it as resolved with a fourth answer that is none of the three.
findings.evidence: 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md:54 — '**Which discriminator is authoritative — photo binding, an owner-assigned nickname, or a WJ-ID suffix — is Q-01, deferred to Step 5 Must-depth.**' Against the same file's :101 — 'Q-01 | ~~When two objects genuinely share a composite key (documented manufacturer reuse), what discriminates them?~~ **RESOLVED** — the **secondary identifying numbers with their locations** (Gibson factory order number, Fender neck-heel/body/pot codes, amp transformer date codes) ... photo binding and nicknames remain weaker fallbacks where no secondary numbers exist.'
findings.forcedInvention: What the record actually stores as the per-object discriminator when two objects share a composite key. An implementer reading the edge-case table treats the choice as undecided among photo binding / nickname / WJ-ID suffix; an implementer reading Q-01 builds secondary identifying numbers as the discriminator with those three as fallbacks.

findings.claim: The locked flag state set gives every state a definite sale-blocking answer except `resolved`, which is 'Per outcome' — and no outcome vocabulary is defined anywhere in the domain, while the transition map routes genuine unresolved ownership disputes into `resolved`.
findings.evidence: 15.02.04-false-flag-dispute-lifecycle.md:43 — '| `resolved` | Dispute reached a terminal external outcome (terminal) | Per outcome | outcome recorded, not adjudicated by platform |', where the same table gives 'Yes (screening match blocks/warns)' for `reported` and 'No' for `contested`, `stale`, `withdrawn` and `recovered`. The state is reachable from a live dispute: :92 — '| Both parties have genuine claims (band split, gear bought jointly) | Not a theft — an ownership dispute wearing a theft flag; routed to domain 24 / 15.01.02 | Flag → `resolved` (routed out); the dispute continues in the ownership-claim surface, not here |'. No enumeration of external outcomes, and no mapping from outcome to blocking, appears in 15.02.04, in 15.02.02-point-of-sale-serial-screening.md, or in the sub-domain index.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether gear whose flag has gone `resolved` is sellable. Because `resolved` is reachable while the underlying ownership dispute is still live elsewhere, one implementer unblocks the listing (the flag reached its terminal state) and another keeps it blocked (the dispute the flag stood for is unresolved) — opposite outcomes for the same record.

findings.claim: Who has standing to file a theft report is stated as still deferred in 15.02.01's edge-case table while both questions it points at are recorded as resolved, and the resolution itself is recorded only inside a struck-through question row citing a 'D-05' that does not exist in that file's Decisions table.
findings.evidence: 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:51 — '| Stolen gear was under someone else's custody (15.08) | Both the owner and the holder may file ... Final standing rules deferred — see Q-01 and 15.08 Q-01. |'. Against the same file's :99 — 'Q-01 | ~~Who has standing to file when ownership and custody differ?~~ **Resolved by DQ-MG-04 / D-05 (2026-07-21):** the owner **or** a party in a custody state `15.08` already enumerates may file, with filing capacity recorded on the flag' and 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:114 — 'Q-01 | ~~Who has standing to report gear stolen...~~ **RESOLVED (D-64 / DQ-MG-04, ratified 2026-07-21)**'. 15.02.01's Decisions table (:90-93) contains only D-01 (bulk flagging by case or rig) and D-02 (police reference optional) — there is no D-05; 15.08's D-05 (:108) is 'Stale custody decays confidence and nudges; it never auto-reverts', a different subject. The ratified standing rule appears in no Decisions table in the domain.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether standing-to-file is settled, and what the binding statement of it is. A reader of the edge-case table treats it as open; a reader of Q-01 treats it as closed but cannot follow the cited D-05 to a decision record, and must decide from prose whether 'a party in a custody state 15.08 already enumerates' means the six custody reasons (loan/service/consignment/hire/in-transit/room-resident, 15.08:32-37) or the record states table that includes `stale` and `disputed` (15.08:70-78) — 15.08:60 says standing under the latter two 'is still open', implying they are in the set that :114 calls 'the six enumerated states'.

That the stage has run is recorded across the domain, e.g. gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:10 'Two structural findings from the Step 5 deepening pass frame everything below' and 15.06.01-rig-definition-signal-chain.md:99 'Deferral re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5.' — the Q rows were re-pointed; these inline markers were not.

findings.claim: Whether a band's outgoing rig spec sheet may disclose gear it holds but does not own is called 'real and unresolved' in the domain cross-cut file, yet it is tracked only by an owner-less marker naming a completed stage, and by no numbered question anywhere.
findings.evidence: 15.06.03-rig-spec-sheet-source-data.md:54 — '| Rig contains gear the user doesn't own (15.08) | The sheet discloses someone else's asset | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |'. gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:395 (CX-15) — '3. **Permission intersection**: Exporting a rig spec (15.06.03) that includes held-not-owned gear discloses someone else's asset — real and unresolved (CX-18 sibling).' 15.06.03's own Q table covers only live-read vs snapshot (Q-01), stage plots (Q-02) and serial stripping (Q-03); 15.06's index Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover oracle viability, unowned rig membership (resolved) and rig entity ownership. The parallel question from the opposite direction is properly tracked — 15.07.03-backline-list-publication.md:120 'Q-02 | Should gear held on loan (15.08) be publishable? ... | Agent | `/create-prd-security`' — which shows the shape the missing row should take.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether held-not-owned rig members appear in an exported spec sheet at all, and whether the owner's consent is required. One implementer exports the whole rig (it is the band's rig); another suppresses or masks borrowed and house gear. The domain has a ratified consent posture for the mirror case (15.08 D-02/D-04) but nothing binds it here.
